title: Version adhesion routing — playtest notes
body:
Purpose:
Quick exploratory notes and a lightweight playbook for how model-version adhesion (what we colloquially call "sticky versions") should interact with routing and the control plane across regions. This is a working doc — experiments, heuristics, and open questions are intentionally messy.

TL;DR:
- Problem: users pin a model version in the registry, but routing policies and multi-region fallbacks can implicitly override behavior. We need simple rules so pinned versions are honored where possible and safe fallbacks are predictable.
- Proposal (high level): implement a 3-tier precedence for routing decisions: explicit pin (user-requested version) -> regional affinity rules (latency/cost constraints) -> compatibility fallback (compatible model variants). Provide a fast probe + preflight check in the control plane before routing to remote region.

Context / motivation:
- Several incident postmortems showed customer workloads getting routed to quantized variants that produced subtle hallucination changes after global fallback kicked in.
- We want deterministic behavior for pinned versions but still need graceful degradation when capacity or hardware incompatibilities occur.

Assumptions:
- Registry contains metadata flags per model-version: supported_kernels (e.g., cuBLAS/Triton), quantized (int8/4), max_seq_len, kv_cache_compatible (boolean), region_blacklist (list).
- Control plane can query a regional capability matrix (what hardware/quantization it supports) with low latency.
- We cannot block requests for >20s while remote model spins up — must return quickly with fallback or reject.

Experiment notes (what we tried in lab):
- Playtest A: honor pin strictly -> return 409 when version unavailable. Outcome: good determinism, lots of errors for canary customers during cold starts.
- Playtest B: honor pin but allow read-only fallback to last-successful-version in same customer namespace. Outcome: fewer errors, subtle behavior drift.
- Playtest C: probe-run: control plane forwards a tiny synthetic request to candidate runtime to check compatibility before routing bulk traffic. Outcome: overhead ~5–12ms per probe, caught 95% kernel mismatches.

Compatibility quick-matrix (hand-drawn, simplified) — rows = model version, columns = region runtime capability

| model_version | region-us-east-1 | region-eu-west-1 | region-ap-south-1 | notes                   |
|--------------:|-----------------:|------------------:|-------------------:|-------------------------:|
| v1.3.2        | gpu-A100:int8    | gpu-A100:int8     | cpu-only           | kv_cache=yes, tuned-kernel|
| v1.4.0        | gpu-A100:int8    | gpu-A100:int4     | gpu-T4:int8         | quantization mismatch EU |
| v2.0.0-ql     | gpu-A100:int4    | gpu-A100:int4     | gpu-T4:int8         | requires ql-kernel v2     |

Heuristic rules (draft):
1) Pin strong: if user pins a version explicitly (model:version in request metadata), try to route to a region+pool that advertises full compatibility. If none available within the latency SLO, return a deterministic fallback decision (see 3).
2) Probe preflight: control plane should attempt a lightweight compatibility probe against candidate runtime (tiny generation / kv cache load) before shifting traffic. If probe fails, mark candidate as incompatible for X minutes.
3) Fallback semantics (in priority order):
   - a) local compatible variant in same region (e.g., same version quantized differently) if registry metadata marks variant as "semantic-equals" and customer tolerance flag = true.
   - b) pinned-version-last-known-in-namespace (safe, but may be older) — only if customer allows historic fallback in their account policy.
   - c) reject with clear error (HTTP 409) when strict_pin policy is enabled on account or route.
4) Telemetry/observable signals: all fallback decisions MUST annotate traces with decision_reason, candidate_pool, probe_latency, and model_compat_checkid so CS and SRE can reconstruct.

Control plane APIs needed (sketch):
- GET /registry/v1/model/{name}/version/{v}/meta -> returns capability keys (string map) and compatibility hints (list of compatible variant ids).
- POST /controlplane/v1/probe -> {region, pool, model, version, probe_id} -> returns pass/fail, latency, kernel_mismatch_flag.
- PATCH /routing/v1/bind -> accept pinned binding with options: {strict:true|false, max_latency_ms, allow_historic:true|false} (affects how fallbacks are chosen).

Multi-region playbook (for platform operators):
- Normal rollout: pin-to-region (preferred region) + allow cross-region fallback=false -> ensures traffic stays local, avoid surprises.
- Emergency: for critical outage, ops can set "allow_cross_region_emergency=true" which permits cross-region routing to best-effort compatible variants. Must be coupled with customer notification if pinned versions are affected.

Open questions / tradeoffs we still need to decide:
- How to encode "semantic-equals" between quantized variants? We currently have manual tags. Could we add lightweight eval checks (BLEU/embedding-distance) as part of registry metadata? Costly.
- Probe cost: per-request preflight is expensive at scale. Should we probe per-candidate pool and cache results for 60s? What TTL?
- Rollout UX: expose a preview endpoint to customers to test candidate fallbacks with a small percentage of golden traffic.
- Backwards compatibility: some older runtime versions accept requests but silently degrade outputs when quantization differs. Need explicit kernel mismatch errors in runtime.

Immediate action items (next week):
- Implement probe endpoint prototype (Marcus) — minimal API, return schema used by routing decision.
- Add "compatibility-tags" field to model registry metadata and populate for v1.4.0 and v2.0.0-ql (Anjali + model-ops).
- Dashboard widget: fallback events/percent by route (Priya) — baseline for alerts.

Notes to self / scratch fragments:
- consider a "soft-pin" mode for dev tenants where we try to honor pin but auto-fallback to avoid noisier errors.
- wallet: look up PLAT-1987 (incident) for example traces.
- remind: doc registry should be authoritative source for kernel capabilities (avoid ad-hoc mapping in control plane).

References and links:
- incident notes: JIRA-PLAT-1987 (linked above)
- related PR: infra#821 (compat probe prototype)
- design sketch: /confluence/PLAT/Model+Registry+Capabilities (internal)

End of playtest dump. Will iterate toward a more formal RFC once probe metrics and dashboard show clear signal.
